newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian shares to resume climb after profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Belgian shares to resume climb after profit-taking.

text.p: The Bel-20 index, distancing itself from gains on most other European markets and ignoring Wall Street's firmer start, suffered from a mild bout of profit-taking on Thursday pushing the index back below the key 2,000-point level.

But dealers said Wall Street's .DJI fresh gains, a strong dollar and dwindling rate increase fears in Europe would launch the Bel-20 higher again. "We think the market is still bullish, it can push above 2,000," said one trader.
The Bel-20 closed down 0.34 percent, or 6.81 points, at 1,998.56 after earlier touching 2,005.23.
It ended a run of seven firmer sessions in a row.
"Some institutional investors wanted to sell but it didn't have much of an impact on the market which is why we are still bullish," a trader said.
Chemical and drugs group UCB, considered too expensive by a number of players, was one of the most prominent victims of profit-taking, dropping 0.17 percent to 89,900 francs.
Chemicals firm Solvay shed 0.56 percent to 22,200 francs but traders said they remained bullish for chemical stocks which could be the driving force behind the bourse's rise in coming months.
"Chemicals should outperform the market because everybody wants them as they're expected to show good figures this year," one trader said.
The star of the day was non-ferrous metals producer Union Miniere which jumped 5.41 percent to 2,340 francs on rising zinc prices.
"We are still bullish about Union Miniere, but we have a buy limit at 2,400 (francs)," one trader said.
Insurer Fortis AG will also be closely monitored after announcing it planned to raise 17 billion Belgian francs by issuing new shares to pay for recent acquisitions.
Analysts said that Fortis AG, which closed down 1.25 percent at 5,530 francs, would probably issue one new share for every ten existing ones.
"Usually when a capital increase is announced the market retreats a bit, but it all depends on the optimism for growth of the group, which in this case is positive," said one trader.
